title: Clay Decker: Escaping The Tang
description:
Clay Decker was one of nine men who survived the loss of USS Tang (SS-306), sunk by her own circular-running torpedo in the Luzon Strait on 24 October 1944. Here he describes escaping the sunken submarine through the forward escape trunk — one of only two times that escape trunk was ever used successfully on a boat like Pampanito.

Decker's story is told in full in Alex Kershaw's "Escape From the Deep," which drew on these interviews as source material.

title: Clay Decker: Tang's History and Captivity (2002)
description:
In this 2002 interview, Clay Decker describes USS Tang's service record, how she came to be sunk by one of her own torpedoes on her fifth war patrol, and his experience as a prisoner of war.

Tang sank more enemy shipping than any other American submarine of the war. Her commanding officer, Richard O'Kane, received the Medal of Honor.
